summary: Helmut Eimer was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Hamburg, Humboldt, and Bonn under Frank-Richard Hamm (~1968–1973). He completed his Promotion at Bonn (~1968–1974) and held a post there from ~1974 to 2001.

Helmut Hoffmann was an Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied in Freiburg, Berlin (Dr. phil.), and Marburg, supervised by Heinrich Lüders. He held posts at the Prussian Academy of Sciences, Munich (1948–1968), and Indiana University (1969–1980).

Helmut Krasser was a Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology scholar who studied at the University of Vienna (Promotion 1981–1989; Habilitation ~1998–2002). He worked at Vienna (~1991–2002), the Austrian Academy of Sciences (~1991–2014), and directed the IKGA (2007–2014).

Helmut Rix was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Würzburg, Heidelberg (PhD 1947–1950), and Tübingen (Habilitation ~1955–1959). He held posts at Tübingen, Augustana-Hochschule Neuendettelsau (1955), the University of Regensburg (1966), and Freiburg as professor (1982–1993).

Helmut Tauscher is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ernst Steinkellner. He has held posts at the University of Vienna (attested 1983, 2010–2015, and 2026) and served as Numata visiting professor at Leiden University.

Helmuth von Glasenapp was an Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tübingen, Munich, Berlin, and Bonn, completing a PhD under Hermann Jacobi. He held posts at Bonn, Berlin, Königsberg (1928–1944), and Tübingen (1946–1959).

Helwig Schmidt-Glintzer is a sinologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Göttingen (~1967–1969) and the University of Munich (~1969–1973), later holding posts at Munich (~1981–1993) and Göttingen (~1993–2015).

Hemchandra Raychaudhuri was an Indologist and historian. He served as Carmichael Professor and Head of the Department of Ancient Indian History and Culture (and later History) at the University of Calcutta, attested in 1939 and 1965.
Hemmige Shriniwasrangachar Biligiri is a linguist and Indologist. He held the post of professor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, attested in 1991 and 2026.

Henepola Gunaratana is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Kelaniya, Buddhist Missionary College, and American University (BA and PhD). His posts include the Buddhist Institute of Kuala Lumpur, Buddhist Vihara Society, Georgetown, and University of Maryland.

Heng Sure is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Oakland University, UC Berkeley, and the Graduate Theological Union (PhD ~1997–2003) under Ronald Y. Nakasone and Hsuan Hua. He has held professorships at GTU, Bond University, and Dharma Realm Buddhist University.

Henk Blezer is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who completed his Doctoraal studies at Leiden University (1987–1997). He held posts as a researcher and lecturer at Leiden (1993–1997, 2002–2008) and worked at the IIAS (1997–2001).

Henk Bodewitz was an Indologist who studied at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda, earning his PhD in 1973. He held posts at Utrecht University (assistant professor 1966; chair of Sanskrit 1976–1992) and Leiden University (associate professor ~1972–1976; professor 1992–2002).

Henri Bergson was a philosopher who studied at Lycée Condorcet, École Normale Supérieure (~1878–1881), and the University of Paris (~1888–1889). He held teaching posts at the lycée David d'Angers (~1881–1883) and the Collège de France (1900–1904).

Henri Cordier was a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology who studied at Lycée Chaptal. He held professorships at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (~1881–1925) and Sciences Po (~1886–1925).

Henri Gaidoz was a linguist who studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and under Albrecht Weber (1865). He held posts teaching geography and ethnography at École Libre des Sciences Politiques (1872–1908) and as Directeur d’études at École Pratique des Hautes Études (1876).

Henri Hubert was a religious studies and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and École Normale Supérieure (~1892–1895). He held posts at the EPHE (~1898–1927), National Archaeological Museum (~1898–1927), and École du Louvre (~1906–1927).

Henri Maspero was a sinology, religious studies, and linguistics scholar who studied under Édouard Chavannes. He worked at the EFEO and held chairs in Sinology at the Collège de France (1918–1945), EPHE (~1919–1944), and the University of Paris/Sorbonne (~1937–1944).
Henri Massé was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He held academic posts at the University of Algiers (~1919–1927) and the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes (~1927–1958).

Henrik Samuel Nyberg was an Iranian, Central Asian, linguistics, and religious studies scholar who studied at Uppsala University in 1908. He taught at Fjellstedt School (~1916–1919) and served as Dozent and Professor in Semitics at Uppsala University (~1919–1956).
